reviewer_notes: Replaces the 2022 to 2023 utility-scale solar moratorium (Sabin REC-0118, held back as lifted; last set to expire Sept. 30, 2023). Opened 2026-10-07: the ordinance text, https://www.cleanenergydistricts.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Linn-County-Utility-Scale-Solar-Siting-Ordinance.pdf , headed 'Prepared by Stephanie Lientz, Linn County Planning & Development' and 'An Ordinance Amending the Code of Ordinances, Linn County, Iowa by modifying provisions in Chapter 107: Article VI Section 107-117 regarding utility scale solar installations and battery energy storage systems, and Article VII Section 107-149 Renewable Energy Overlay District, and Article VII Table 107-147-1 regarding battery energy storage systems, and Article IX Section 107-180 definitions'. This copy leaves the ordinance number and the Gazette publication date blank. It records Planning and Zoning Commission Aug. 16, 2023; public hearing and first consideration Sept. 5, 2023; second consideration Sept. 13, 2023; third consideration and final passage Sept. 20, 2023. Also opened: The Gazette, https://www.thegazette.com/local-government/government-notes-linn-county-supervisors-pass-solar-ordinance/ : the Board of Supervisors 'unanimously adopted tighter restrictions for utility-scale solar installations', approved the score card 2-1 (Running-Marquardt and Rogers for, Zumbach against), and 'The changes won't apply to previously approved projects'. Corrected against the source: added the 50 dBA night limit (the row had only 55 dBA daytime); added the battery storage 500 ft setback from off-site occupied structures and the 120 ft stream setback for storage; added the CSP prohibition; replaced 'Acreage caps: none found' with the 160-acre fenced-array wildlife corridor rule; added battery_storage to technology, since the ordinance regulates battery energy storage systems too; source_url changed from the Sept. 20, 2023 minutes, which were not read, to the ordinance text that was. Removed, since neither document read contains it: that land rated 65 CSR or above is discouraged through the scorecard (the scorecard itself was not found; the Gazette says only that supervisors discussed the points deducted for higher-CSR areas). Not read: the county pages (linncountyiowa.gov answers with a Cloudflare challenge, HTTP 403, so allowing the host does not help) and the minutes. Not found: the ordinance number and the Gazette publication date. CSP prohibition and the corridor rule are not in the restriction scoring vocabulary, so they sit in mechanism_detail; listing 'ban/prohibition' would score the whole instrument as a solar ban. Severity 2 by the README rule (largest solar setback 300 ft, under 1,000 ft).
description: Linn County replaced its utility-scale solar moratorium with siting rules in its Unified Development Code: solar equipment 300 ft from dwellings unless the owner waives it, 120 ft from perennial streams and ditches, 50 ft from property lines in the Renewable Energy overlay district; battery storage 200 ft from property lines and rights-of-way and 500 ft from off-site occupied structures unless waived; 55 dBA day and 50 dBA night noise limits; RE overlay rezoning and a passing score on the county's solar scorecard. Concentrating solar power is prohibited, and fenced arrays over 160 acres need a wildlife corridor.
mechanism_detail: setback: solar panels, structures and electrical equipment (excluding fences and interconnection lines) 300 ft from dwellings unless the owner waives it in writing (recorded); 120 ft from the centerline of perennial stream corridors and open ditches; 50 ft from property lines in the Renewable Energy overlay district (may be reduced to zero next to another overlay use). Battery energy storage: 200 ft from a property line or right-of-way; 500 ft from the nearest property line including an occupied structure off the subject property, reducible to 200 ft by a recorded, notarized waiver from that owner; 120 ft from perennial stream corridors and open ditches; sited inside a new solar facility when built with one. overlay_zone: rezoning to the Renewable Energy overlay district and the minimum passing threshold on the Linn County Utility Scale Solar Scorecard. noise_limit: hourly average 55 dBA by day (sunrise to sunset) and 50 dBA at night (sunset to sunrise) at the occupied dwelling of an adjacent residential property, or ambient Leq plus 5 dBA where ambient is higher; neighbours may waive in writing. Other: concentrating solar power (CSP) systems prohibited; fenced array areas over 160 acres require a wildlife corridor; panels at least 24 in. above ground at maximum tilt.
evidence_text: Solar panels, structures, and electrical equipment, excluding fences and power lines for interconnection, shall be kept a minimum of three hundred (300) feet from dwellings, unless the property owner waives the setback. Waiver must be in writing and recorded.
